Your S$138,574 time deposit matures on 2026-11-17. For reference, indicative promotional SGD rates for S$100,000 - S$249,999 are 0.2500% for 12 - 15 mths and 0.5000% for 18 mth; I will confirm current terms, as promotions apply to fresh funds placed at a branch.

points.text: Thank you for coming in, Joanne. Since your home loan lock-in ends soon and you've asked before about earning more on idle cash, I thought we could review both today.
Your home loan (H00620) has S$706,488 outstanding on a 'Short-term fixed' package, and the lock-in ends on 2026-11-08, which is 33 days away. This is a good time to review your options.

Our refinancing packages include short-term fixed rates from 2.38% for the first year, variable rates from 1.75% for the first year, and Fixed Deposit-linked rates at the 36-month Fixed Deposit Mortgage Rate + 1.23% for the first 3 years. These are indicative and I will confirm current terms.

The trade-off: fixed rates give fixed monthly payments and protect you from rate fluctuations for the first 1-2 years but tend to be higher, while variable rates are lower but can change with the OCBC board rate.

You have S$50,402 in your Bonus+ Savings Account. The 360 Account gives bonus interest on the first S$70,000, for example 1.2% per year when you credit a salary of at least S$2,000 through GIRO, plus base interest of 0.05% per year. These rates are indicative and I will confirm current terms.

If some cash isn't needed soon, a Singapore Dollar time deposit is another option; indicative promotional rates for >$50,000 - S$99,999 are 0.2500% for 12 - 15 mths and 0.6500% for 36 mth. Promotions need fresh funds placed at a branch, and I will confirm current terms.
What matters more to you for the next home loan package: predictable monthly payments or the lowest possible starting rate?
How much of your savings might you need in the next year or so, and how much could be set aside longer?
You mentioned a fall-below fee last month. Can you tell me more about what happened so we can avoid it going forward?

The client complained about a fall-below fee on 2026-09-04; note the 360 Account has a S$3,000 minimum average daily balance and a S$2 fee (waived for the first year), indicative only. Also, the time deposit promotion requires fresh funds, so moving existing OCBC balances may not qualify.

Avoid SIBOR-based refinancing packages in the product data; they are stale as SIBOR has been retired in Singapore. The 360 insure/invest bonus involves investment or insurance products, so suitability must be assessed first (risk profile on file: Balanced).
